pr_title: Check for unassigned shards on node shutdown
pr_body:
`TransportGetShutdownStatusAction` has few checks that prevents a node from being shut down if there are shards without a copy which can't be moved. 

With this PR we also check if the node has unassigned primary shards and if it does, we return the STALLED status and prevent the node from being shut down. To ensure that the node was the last one to hold a copy of the unassigned shard, we check the `org.elasticsearch.cluster.routing.UnassignedInfo#lastAllocatedNodeId`.

- [x] Figure out what kind of integration tests I need to add

Closes #88635
pr_comments: Hi @grcevski, I've created a changelog YAML for you.
Do we need any sort of timeout so that a node isnt left STALLED indefinitely if its cluster state gets out of sync & isnt updated? Or is that handled elsewhere in the infrastructure?

> Do we need any sort of timeout so that a node isnt left STALLED indefinitely if its cluster state gets out of sync & isnt updated? Or is that handled elsewhere in the infrastructure?

It should be up to the infrastructure to implement timeouts, if they don't want to permanently wait for a stalled node. We just need to ensure we don't cause data loss, if it's intentional by any orchestrator then they can always shutdown a stalled node.

issue_context.title: Add a check for unassigned shards residing on the node being removed in the shutdown status check
issue_context.body:
`TransportGetShutdownStatusAction` has a few checks that prevents the node from being shut down if there are shards without a copy that we can't move. We should also check that whether the node has unassigned shard and if it does, return the `STALLED` status and prevent the node from being shut down.

Relates #73873, #78578
comments: Also check that any unassigned shards did not reside lastly on one of the nodes being shut down, else return STALLED. cc @idegtiarenko

Also logically thinking, shutdown should be done safely.
That said, if a shutdown can result in a red cluster (from either green or yellow), then it should fail. 
Or alternatively, node shutdown API should also check cluster health, and if it's red (no matter at the beginning of the plan it's green or yellow), it should fail.

Otherwise, it causes data loss. 

(cc @idegtiarenko )

> Or alternatively, node shutdown API should also check cluster health, and if it's red (no matter at the beginning of the plan it's green or yellow), it should fail.

I do not think that we should rely on a cluster health in this case. Instead we should check the `org.elasticsearch.cluster.routing.UnassignedInfo#lastAllocatedNodeId` on every unallocated primary shard and only stall if it is the node we are trying to permanently shutdown.

We should be able to shut down a node in a red cluster if the node is not holding any last copy of the data. It is also okay to shut down a node in a yellow cluster as the yellow shard could be migrated somewhere else and the replicas could be rebuild from the new primary.
We'll use the approach @idegtiarenko suggested and implement that. Before we say we are in progress of shutting down we'll run the checks on lastAllocatedNodeId.

I wrote some additional tests and I had to modify the condition slightly, it's not enough to check for primary shard always, what I did instead is ask if this unassigned shard is found somewhere else, on a node that's not shutting down. So primary or not found elsewhere. Does that make sense?

review_comments: I needed to move this method over from the base class, because the subclass uses different allocators. The Gateway allocator keeps track of the unassigned shards, so it's the one that would explain the shard movement.
